\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.Randomized.RandomWalkPad}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Padded neighbor]
\lean{Randomized.padNbr}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p039-b001}
\label{Randomized.padNbr}
\leanok
Let $r$ be a decidable relation on the vertices $0,\\ldots,n-1$. For a vertex $v$ and
an index $i<D$, define its padded neighbor to be the vertex with index $i$ if $i<n$ and
$v$ is related to that vertex; otherwise define it to be $v$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Padded Neighbor Characterization]
\lean{Randomized.padNbr_eq_iff}
\label{Randomized.padNbr_eq_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.padNbr}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,D\in\mathbb{N}$, let $r$ be a relation on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$u,v\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be distinct. For every $i\in\{0,\ldots,D-1\}$, the padded
neighbor of $u$ at index $i$ equals $v$ if and only if $i=v$ and $r(u,v)$ holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Count of Padded Neighbors]
\lean{Randomized.card_padNbr_eq}
\label{Randomized.card_padNbr_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.padNbr, Randomized.padNbr_eq_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,D$ be natural numbers, let $r$ be a relation on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and suppose
$n\le D$. For distinct vertices $u,v$, the number of indices $i\in\{0,\ldots,D-1\}$
whose padded neighbor of $u$ is $v$ is $1$ if $r(u,v)$ holds and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padded regular multigraph]
\lean{Randomized.padGraph}
\statementsource{Vad12}{
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p038-b004,
  pdf-bf2ce5422088-p039-b001
}
\label{Randomized.padGraph}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph, Randomized.card_padNbr_eq, Randomized.padNbr}
Let $r$ be a symmetric relation on the finite vertex set $0,\\ldots,n-1$, and let $D$
be a natural number with $n\\le D$. The padded regular multigraph has degree $D$ and
assigns to each vertex and each of its $D$ edge slots the padded neighbor; its edge
multiplicities are symmetric.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Adjacency in the padded graph]
\lean{Randomized.padGraph_adj_iff}
\label{Randomized.padGraph_adj_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.Adj, Randomized.padGraph, Randomized.padNbr, Randomized.padNbr_eq_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r$ be a decidable symmetric relation on the finite set $\text{Fin}(n)$, and let $D$
be a natural number with $n \le D$. In the padded multigraph defined from $r$ using
degree parameter $D$, vertices $u,v \in \text{Fin}(n)$ are adjacent exactly when $u=v$
or $r(u,v)$ holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reachability in the padded graph]
\lean{Randomized.padGraph_reflTransGen_iff}
\label{Randomized.padGraph_reflTransGen_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.Adj, Randomized.padGraph, Randomized.padGraph_adj_iff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $r$ be a decidable symmetric relation on $\text{Fin}(n)$, and let $D$ be a natural
number with $n \le D$. For any $s,t \in \text{Fin}(n)$, there is a finite sequence of
padded-graph adjacency steps from $s$ to $t$ (allowing a sequence of length zero) if and
only if there is a finite sequence of $r$-related steps from $s$ to $t$, also allowing
length zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padding degree]
\lean{Randomized.padDegree}
\label{Randomized.padDegree}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, define the padding degree to be $2^{\\operatorname{size}(n)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Padding degree bound]
\lean{Randomized.le_padDegree}
\label{Randomized.le_padDegree}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.padDegree}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, $n\leq 2^{\operatorname{size}(n)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Padding degree bound]
\lean{Randomized.padDegree_le}
\label{Randomized.padDegree_le}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.padDegree}
\difficulty{4}
For every positive natural number $n$, the power of $2$ whose exponent is the binary
length of $n$ is at most $2n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Success probability of a padded graph walk]
\lean{Randomized.three_quarters_le_randProb_padWalk}
\label{Randomized.three_quarters_le_randProb_padWalk}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hits, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.randProb_hits_decodeIdx, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.three_quarters_le_hitProb, Randomized.decodeIdx, Randomized.le_padDegree, Randomized.padDegree, Randomized.padDegree_le, Randomized.padGraph, Randomized.padGraph_reflTransGen_iff, Randomized.randProb}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $r$ be a symmetric relation on the vertices
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $s,t$ be vertices such that $t$ is reachable from $s$ by a
finite sequence of $r$-steps. Set $D=2^{\operatorname{size}(n)}$, where
$\operatorname{size}(n)$ is the binary size of $n$, and fix a bijection from the binary
words of length $\operatorname{size}(n)$ to the $D$ edge slots. Choose uniformly a
binary word of length $100n^4\operatorname{size}(n)$, decode it into $100n^4$ edge slots
using this bijection, and walk from $s$ in the padded undirected regular multigraph
determined by $r$, accepting if the visited vertices include $t$. The probability of
acceptance is at least $3/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero probability of reaching an inaccessible vertex]
\lean{Randomized.randProb_padWalk_eq_zero}
\label{Randomized.randProb_padWalk_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hitProb_eq_zero_of_not_reachable, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.hits, Randomized.RegularMultigraph.randProb_hits_decodeIdx, Randomized.decodeIdx, Randomized.padGraph, Randomized.padGraph_reflTransGen_iff, Randomized.randProb}
\difficulty{4}
Let $V=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and let $r$ be a symmetric relation on $V$. Suppose vertices
$s,t\in V$ are such that there is no finite sequence of $r$-steps from $s$ to $t$,
allowing a sequence of length zero. Let $D\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $n\le D$, let
$b\in\mathbb{N}$, and fix a bijection from Boolean strings of length $b$ to
$\{0,\ldots,D-1\}$. Form the $D$-slot graph on $V$ by using each slot to move along its
corresponding $r$-edge when that edge exists, and otherwise leaving the vertex
unchanged. For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, if a uniformly random Boolean string of length
$kb$ is split into $k$ consecutive blocks of length $b$ and decoded as slot choices, the
probability that the resulting walk starting at $s$ visits $t$ is zero.
\end{theorem}
